# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy v2

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## Constraints
- Time: evenings and weekends only
- Budget: up to $2,000 of personal savings this year
- Employment: Dorrance Logistics contract restricts public statements and outside roles.
  - Do NOT publish anything with my name on it (posts, letters, press) until the annual
    outside-activities disclosure is filed (due 30 November 2026) and I've spoken to HR.
  - Outside roles and paid work must be disclosed and may need advance approval.
- Skills: writing, basic Python; not a researcher or engineer by trade

## Approach (replacing abandoned Strategy v1)
Strategy v1 was "launch loudly, email everyone, get press, raise money fast, figure out the work later" — abandoned because it was backwards.

v2: Start small, stay private until HR clearance, build concrete output, then go public.

Phase 1 (now – Nov 30): Infrastructure + private exploration
- Secure domain (halcyonthreshold.org renewed through Nov 2027) ✅
- Set up repo and working documents (private)
- Explore grant/funding options (Emberfall rapid grants, Compute Commons credits)
- Accept volunteer help (Priya Raman) for concrete, non-public tasks
- File Dorrance outside-activities disclosure

Phase 2 (Dec – Jan): First public output
- Publish website after HR clearance
- Choose one concrete workstream (reading group / small grants / evals / writing)
- Decide whether to apply for Emberfall grant

## Workstream options (unsorted, to be triaged)
1. A reading group for people new to AI safety
2. A small-grants / micro-funding thing for neglected projects
3. Evals for something nobody is measuring
4. A newsletter (probably too many already — deprioritized)

## People
- Priya Raman (priya.raman@fastmail.com) — data analyst, ~5 hrs/week, offered help
- Idris Bellamy (grants@emberfallfund.org) — Emberfall Fund program officer
- Lena Fischbach — interpretability researcher, busy
- Tomasz Wrona — Corvid Institute, governance
- Asha Venkataraman — Alignment Commons forum moderator
- Daniel Oyelaran — Compute Commons, compute grants
- Noor Haddad — ex-lab engineer, "don't quote me"
- Sam Whitlock — indie evals person

# Halcyon Threshold — Emberfall Rapid Grant Proposal (DRAFT)

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale (individual, operating as Halcyon Threshold)
**Round:** Emberfall Fund Rapid Grants (closes 30 November 2026)
**Amount requested:** TBD ($5k–$25k typical)
**Format:** Two-page proposal + simple budget (per Idris Bellamy's email)

> NOTE: This draft is private. Do not submit until the Dorrance outside-activities
> disclosure has been filed and HR has been consulted, per Morgan's employment constraint.

---

## 1. What you'll do

Halcyon Threshold is a small independent initiative focused on improving the outcome of
superintelligent AI's arrival. Founded November 2026 by Morgan Hale.

Initial workstream (to be confirmed after HR clearance and volunteer onboarding):
- A volunteer-run reading group and curated resource list for people new to AI safety,
  focused on making technical and governance concepts accessible to non-specialists.
- Small, targeted micro-grants ($250–$1,000) for neglected AI-safety-adjacent projects
  that fall between the cracks of larger funders.

All work performed evenings and weekends; no full-time staff.

## 2. Why you

Morgan Hale has been following AI safety since 2025, organized a local meetup talk on
superintelligence risk (November 2026), and has a network of contacts in research,
governance, and independent evals. Skills: writing, basic Python, project coordination.

Constraints: evenings and weekends only; up to $2,000 personal savings available this
year. Seeking external funding to extend the budget and compensate volunteer time.

## 3. What it costs (draft budget)

| Item | Amount |
|------|--------|
| Domain registration (halcyonthreshold.org, 1 yr) | $14.99 |
| Website hosting (Pagewell Pro, if needed) | $20/month |
| Volunteer compensation (Priya Raman, ~5 hrs/wk @ $25/hr, 3 months) | $1,500 |
| Micro-grants pool (3–5 grants of $250–$1,000) | $2,500–$5,000 |
| Miscellaneous (software, reference materials) | $200 |
| **Total** | **~$4,235–$6,735** |
